coverage: Complete play in both English editions: named cast, speaker roles, dramatic roles, identifiable unnamed figures and named cultural references.

entities.name: Hermia
entities.body: Egeus’s daughter, in love with Lysander.

entities.name: Lysander
entities.body: The young Athenian whom Hermia loves.

entities.name: Helena
entities.body: Hermia’s friend, in love with Demetrius.

entities.name: Demetrius
entities.body: The suitor Egeus wants Hermia to marry.

snapshots.body: The young Athenian who now declares his love for Helena.

entities.name: Theseus
entities.body: Duke of Athens, engaged to Hippolyta.

entities.name: Hippolyta
entities.body: Queen of the Amazons, engaged to Theseus.

entities.name: Egeus
entities.body: Hermia’s father.

entities.name: Philostrate
entities.body: Theseus’s master of revels, responsible for entertainments.

entities.name: Nick Bottom
entities.body: The weaver in Peter Quince’s amateur acting company.

snapshots.body: The weaver and amateur actor, now wearing an ass’s head through Puck’s magic.
The weaver and amateur actor, restored to his human appearance.

entities.name: Peter Quince
entities.body: The carpenter who organizes the amateur players.

entities.name: Francis Flute
entities.body: The bellows-mender in Quince’s acting company.

entities.name: Tom Snout
entities.body: The tinker in Quince’s acting company.

entities.name: Snug
entities.body: The joiner in Quince’s acting company.

entities.name: Robin Starveling
entities.body: The tailor in Quince’s acting company.

entities.name: Oberon
entities.body: King of the fairies and husband of Titania.

entities.name: Titania
entities.body: Queen of the fairies and wife of Oberon.

entities.name: Puck
entities.body: Oberon’s mischievous fairy servant, also called Robin Goodfellow.

entities.name: The fairy
entities.body: A fairy serving Titania who meets Puck in the wood.

entities.name: The first singing fairy
entities.body: One of the fairies singing Titania to sleep.

entities.name: The second fairy
entities.body: Another fairy attending Titania as she sleeps.

entities.name: Peaseblossom
entities.body: One of Titania’s attendant fairies.

entities.name: Cobweb
entities.body: One of Titania’s attendant fairies.

entities.name: Moth
entities.body: One of Titania’s attendant fairies.

entities.name: Mustardseed
entities.body: One of Titania’s attendant fairies.

entities.name: Titania’s fairies
entities.body: The fairy attendants who sing and serve Titania.

entities.name: The amateur players
entities.body: Quince’s company of Athenian craftsmen.

entities.name: The Indian boy
entities.body: The young child in Titania’s care, whom Oberon wants as his attendant.

entities.name: The boy’s mother
entities.body: The mortal woman from India who was Titania’s friend and follower.

entities.name: The Indian king
entities.body: The unnamed king from whom Puck says the boy was taken.

entities.name: Pyramus
entities.body: The male lover in the amateur players’ story of Pyramus and Thisbe.

entities.name: Thisbe
entities.body: The female lover in the amateur players’ story of Pyramus and Thisbe.

entities.name: Wall
entities.body: The wall personified as a speaking part in the amateur play.

entities.name: Lion
entities.body: The lion portrayed in the amateur play.

entities.name: Moonshine
entities.body: Moonlight personified as a part in the amateur play.

entities.name: Prologue
entities.body: The speaker who introduces the amateur play.

entities.name: Nedar
entities.body: Helena’s father.

entities.name: Cupid
entities.body: The god of love, represented with a bow and arrows.

entities.name: Venus
entities.body: The goddess of love.

entities.name: Diana
entities.body: The goddess of the hunt and chastity, associated with the moon.

entities.name: Dido
entities.body: The queen of Carthage in the story of Aeneas.

entities.name: Aeneas
entities.body: The Trojan hero loved by Dido.

entities.name: Hercules
entities.body: The legendary hero famed for his strength; Bottom calls him Ercles.

entities.name: Apollo
entities.body: The god associated with music and the sun; Bottom calls him Phibbus.

entities.name: The Fates
entities.body: The mythological powers who govern mortal destiny.

entities.name: Corin
entities.body: The shepherd identity Titania says Oberon has assumed.

entities.name: Phillida
entities.body: The woman Titania says Oberon courted as Corin.

entities.name: Perigenia
entities.body: A woman associated with Theseus in Greek legend.

entities.name: Aegles
entities.body: One of the women Oberon names among Theseus’s former loves.

entities.name: Ariadne
entities.body: The Cretan princess associated with Theseus.

entities.name: Antiopa
entities.body: An Amazon associated with Theseus in Greek legend.

entities.name: Hiems
entities.body: Winter imagined as an aged person.

entities.name: Neptune
entities.body: The Roman god of the sea.

entities.name: Daphne
entities.body: The nymph pursued by Apollo in Greek mythology.

entities.name: Philomel
entities.body: A poetic name for the nightingale, recalling the myth of Philomela.

entities.name: Ninus
entities.body: The legendary Assyrian king whose tomb is the lovers’ meeting place in the amateur play.

entities.name: Mistress Squash
entities.body: The mother Bottom jokingly gives Peaseblossom, playing on the fairy’s name.

entities.name: Master Peascod
entities.body: The father Bottom jokingly gives Peaseblossom; Peascod means a pea pod.

entities.name: Aurora
entities.body: The Roman goddess of dawn.

entities.name: Cadmus
entities.body: The legendary founder of Thebes, recalled as a hunting companion.

entities.name: Saint Valentine
entities.body: The saint whose feast day was associated with birds pairing and lovers.

entities.name: The Centaurs
entities.body: The half-human, half-horse creatures of Greek myth.

entities.name: The Bacchanals
entities.body: The frenzied followers of the wine god, mentioned in a proposed entertainment.

entities.name: Orpheus
entities.body: The legendary musician meant by the Thracian singer in the proposed entertainment.

entities.name: The Muses
entities.body: The nine goddesses of poetry, music and the arts.

entities.name: Learning
entities.body: Learning personified in one of the proposed entertainments.

entities.name: Jove
entities.body: Another name for Jupiter, king of the Roman gods.

entities.name: Leander
entities.body: The mythic lover of Hero, called Limander in the amateur play.

entities.name: Hero
entities.body: The woman loved by Leander in Greek legend, mistakenly called Helen by Thisbe.

entities.name: Cephalus
entities.body: The husband of Procris in Greek legend, called Shafalus by the players.

entities.name: Procris
entities.body: The wife of Cephalus in Greek legend, called Procrus by the players.

entities.name: Hecate
entities.body: The goddess associated with night and magic.

entities.name: Helen of Troy
entities.body: The legendary beauty invoked by Theseus.
